title: Derived morphism sheaves evaluate on weakly contractible pro-etale affines
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $B$ a finite commutative ring, and $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}\to X_{\mathrm{et}}$ the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $E\in D(B)$ be bounded with finite $B$-module cohomology, and let $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ be bounded with finite locally constant cohomology [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\underline E$ for its constant sheaf complex [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Define $\mathcal H_{E,K}$ and $\mathcal I_{E,K}$ by sheafifying, on the etale site, the presheaves $V\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{D(V_{\mathrm{et}},B)}(\underline E|_V,K|_V)$ and $V\mapsto\operatorname{Isom}_{D(V_{\mathrm{et}},B)}(\underline E|_V,K|_V)$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For every affine object $U\to X$ weakly contractible for $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, meaning that every epimorphism of sheaves of sets is surjective on sections over $U$, there are canonical bijections
$$
 (\nu_X^*\mathcal H_{E,K})(U)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},B)}(\underline E|_U,(\nu_X^*K)|_U),\qquad
 (\nu_X^*\mathcal I_{E,K})(U)\cong\operatorname{Isom}_{D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},B)}(\underline E|_U,(\nu_X^*K)|_U).
$$
Here restriction is to the localized pro-etale site over $U$, identified with $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$. The bijections extend pullback of actual etale-local morphisms, preserve identity morphisms and composition whenever defined, and are natural in $E,K$ and restriction between such objects. For a homomorphism $B\to C$ of finite commutative rings for which $E_C=E\otimes_B^L C$ and $K_C=K\otimes_B^L C$ remain bounded with the corresponding finite cohomology hypotheses, they commute with derived scalar extension: the map of pulled-back morphism or isomorphism sheaves induced by $f\mapsto f\otimes_B^L C$ evaluates to the same operation on actual derived morphisms. No finite Tor dimension is assumed.

proof.text: The finite ring $B$ is Noetherian: every ideal is generated by its finitely many elements. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion] makes $E$ pseudo-coherent, and [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] supplies a finite-free complex $P$ representing $E$, with $P^i=0$ for $i>b$. The boundedness of $K$ and [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] supply a representative $N$ with $N^j=0$ for $j<a$. Constant presheaves preserve exact sequences objectwise, so exact module sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] makes the constant-module functor exact. In particular $\underline P$ represents $\underline E$. Exact slice restriction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] and exact comparison inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] preserve these representatives and bounds. All sites and their slices are taken small in the larger module universe of [def-weil-size-convention].

proof.text: A constant sheaf of sets with value $S$ is the coproduct of $S$ copies of the final sheaf: this is the sheafification of the same identity for constant presheaves. Geometric inverse image preserves coproducts as a left adjoint and preserves the final object and finite products. It therefore carries constant sheaves to constant sheaves, with their addition and scalar actions, since these operations are maps between finite powers. Apply this to $\nu_X^*$. For slice restriction, use [lem-weil-pbc-site-constant-restriction], whose statement gives the canonical constant-module isomorphism on the slice, compatible with constant sections and linear maps. These are the canonical coefficient and constant-object identifications: on each constant section they act as the identity. Thus finite free terms remain the corresponding finite free terms on the other site or slice.

proof.text:
Put $M=R\mathcal Hom_{B_X}(\underline E,K)$ on the etale site. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-bounded-free-rhom-model] to $(\underline P,N)$. Its degree-$n$ model $T$ has only the indices $a-n\leq i\leq b$. For $P^i=B^{r_i}$, the sheaf-Hom definition identifies $\mathcal Hom(\underline{P^i},N^{i+n})$ with $(N^{i+n})^{r_i}$: a map is determined by the images of the $r_i$ standard basis vectors. The same formula holds after any slice restriction or $
u_X^*$. These functors preserve finite products, and exactness preserves cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms. The matrices of $d_P$ and the maps $d_N$ give exactly the same differential $d_Nf-(-1)^nf d_P$ on both sides. Applying the same model theorem on the pro-etale site therefore gives the canonical comparison $
u_X^*M\simeq R\mathcal Hom(\underline E,
u_X^*K)$. On slices its restriction is the derived internal Hom of the restricted objects, by this same termwise calculation. The model vanishes for $n<a-b$, so it is bounded below even though $P$ may be unbounded to the left. The comparison is the canonical sheaf map constructed from local pullback in [def-weil-pbc-derived-morphism-sheaf-comparison]; its specified slice identifications are used throughout.

proof.text:
Evaluation over the weakly contractible $U$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-wcontractible-affine-evaluation-colimits]. In a resolution $
u_X^*M	o J$ used to compute derived sections, evaluation preserves the quasi-isomorphism: exactness makes its evaluated cohomology equal to evaluated sheaf cohomology. Consequently $H^0(R\Gamma(U,
u_X^*M))=H^0(
u_X^*M)(U)$. Apply [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] on the slice and the model's slice calculation to identify the left side with the actual derived Hom in the first displayed bijection. The site and coefficient identification with $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], since $U$ is an object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. This proves the Hom bijection.

proof.text: For the Isom assertion consider all four ordered pairs among $\underline E,K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-derived-local-constancy], there is an etale covering on which $K$ is constant with bounded finite coefficient model. On each covering member, steps 1-5 apply to all four pairs: each source is a bounded finite coefficient complex and each target is bounded below. They identify the pullback of its etale morphism sheaf with the degree-zero cohomology sheaf of its pro-etale derived internal Hom. These local comparisons agree on overlaps: every comparison is induced by pullback of actual derived morphisms, as checked in step 5, and restrictions give the same map on each presheaf class. Since the pulled-back covering is a covering, the local comparisons glue to an isomorphism for each of the four morphism sheaves. No claim that a local constant model is perfect is used.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant; canonical local finite-diagonal comparisons

proof.text: For any of these four pro-etale pairs $(A,D)$, choose a representative $L$ of $A$ and a K-injective representative $J$ of $D$. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], the internal Hom is represented by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L,J)$. Its restriction to the slice at $U$ is the Hom complex of the restrictions: on every $V\to U$, each sheaf-Hom factor is $\operatorname{Hom}(L^i|_V,J^{i+n}|_V)$, products are sectionwise, and both differentials are $d_Jf-(-1)^nf d_L$. By [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], $J|_U$ remains K-injective, so this is also the derived internal Hom on the slice. Exact evaluation [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-wcontractible-affine-evaluation-colimits] identifies its degree-zero sheaf cohomology evaluated on $U$ with degree-zero derived sections, exactly as in step 6. Now [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] on that small slice identifies these sections with actual derived Hom. This gives Hom bijections on $U$ for all four pairs. The comparisons preserve identities and composition: pullback on derived categories preserves them, the presheaf operations sheafify to the same operations on classes, and evaluation takes a class to the actual map representing it.

The Isom presheaf identifies with the presheaf of pairs $(f,h)$ in the two opposite Hom presheaves satisfying $hf=1_{\underline E}$ and $fh=1_K$. Its projection to $f$ is injective: if $h,h'$ are inverses then $h=h(fh')=(hf)h'=h'$. It is surjective onto the isomorphisms by the definition of an inverse. This is a finite-limit description using the four Hom presheaves, their composition maps and identity sections. Sheafification preserves that description by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact]; geometric inverse image preserves it by [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]; and sections preserve it because limits of sheaves of sets are computed sectionwise. Step 8 identifies the resulting inverse pairs with pairs of actual mutually inverse derived maps on $U$. This proves the Isom bijection. Its compatibility with composition and identities follows from the corresponding compatibility of those same maps in step 8.

source.place: Tag 00WJ (sites.tex, lemma-sheafification-exact); elementary finite-limit inverse-pair calculation

proof.text:
Naturality in the two variables and slice restriction follows from the canonical map taking an actual derived morphism to its internal-Hom class: precomposition, postcomposition and restriction act on that same map, and the identifications above commute with them. For $B	o C$ as in the statement, the derived tensor-pullback isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identifies $
u_X^*(F\otimes_B^L C)$ with $(
u_X^*F)\otimes_B^L C$, naturally in $F$ and therefore in actual derived maps $f$. Thus on localized etale morphisms the two routes send $f$ to the very same map $(
u_X^*f)\otimes_B^L C$. Sheafify this equality; the canonical actual-morphism-to-sheaf-class maps on the pro-etale site respect the tensor functor, so the resulting square of morphism sheaves commutes. Evaluation on $U$ and the Hom bijections already proved identify its bottom map with actual derived scalar extension. The inverse-pair description of step 9 gives the same square for Isom, since a functor carries inverse pairs to inverse pairs. Apply the Hom computation over $C$ using the assumed boundedness of $E_C,K_C$; do not tensor the $B$-Hom complex to claim a base-change isomorphism for internal Hom. No Tor-dimension assumption is used.
